Expressions, Variables, and Properties: Variable
A letter or symbol representing an unknown or changing value
Coefficient
The number multiplied by a variable in a term
Constant
A term with a fixed value and no variable
Like terms
Terms with the same variable raised to the same power
Commutative property
Order does not change the result when adding or multiplying
Associative property
Grouping does not change the result when adding or multiplying
Distributive property
Multiplying a sum means multiplying each term: a(b + c) = ab + ac
Evaluate an expression
Substitute given values for the variables and simplify
Order of operations
Parentheses, exponents, multiplication and division, then addition and subtraction
Term
A single number, variable, or product of numbers and variables in an expression
Solving Linear Equations: Equation
A statement that two expressions are equal
Solution of an equation
A value for the variable that makes the equation true
Inverse operations
Operations that undo each other, such as addition and subtraction
Isolate the variable
Get the variable alone on one side of the equation
Identity equation
An equation true for every value, giving a result like 3 = 3
No-solution equation
An equation true for no value, giving a false result like 5 = 2
Literal equation
An equation with several variables, often solved for one of them
Multi-step equation
An equation requiring more than one inverse operation to solve
Checking a solution
Substituting your answer back in to confirm both sides match
Cross multiplication
Solving a proportion by multiplying each numerator by the other denominator
Inequalities and Compound Inequalities: Inequality
A statement comparing values with <, >, less than or equal, or greater than or equal
Flipping the inequality sign
Required when multiplying or dividing both sides by a negative number
Open circle
Graph marker showing the endpoint is not included, used for < and >
Closed circle
Graph marker showing the endpoint is included, used for the or-equal-to symbols
Compound inequality
Two inequalities joined by AND or OR
Conjunction (AND)
A compound inequality where both conditions must be true, giving an overlap
Disjunction (OR)
A compound inequality where either condition can be true, giving a union
Interval notation
Writing a solution set with brackets and parentheses, such as [2, 5)
Absolute value inequality
An inequality containing an absolute value, which splits into two cases
Solution set
All values that satisfy an inequality
Introduction to Functions: A relation where each input has exactly one output
The set of all possible input values
The set of all possible output values
A graph is a function if no vertical line crosses it more than once
Writing f(x) to name the output of function f at input x
The output, usually y, which depends on the input
Any set of ordered pairs, whether or not it is a function
Data made of separate, countable values
Data that can take any value within a range
Linear Functions and Graphing: Slope
Rate of change, calculated as rise over run
y-intercept
The point where a line crosses the y-axis, where x equals 0
x-intercept
The point where a line crosses the x-axis, where y equals 0
Slope-intercept form
y = mx + b, where m is slope and b is the y-intercept
Point-slope form
y - y1 = m(x - x1), built from one point and the slope
Standard form
Ax + By = C, useful for finding both intercepts quickly
Parallel lines
Lines with equal slopes that never intersect
Perpendicular lines
Lines whose slopes are negative reciprocals, meeting at 90 degrees
Positive slope
A line rising from left to right
Zero slope
A horizontal line, where y stays constant
Undefined slope
A vertical line, where the run is zero
Rate of change
How much the output changes per unit change in the input
Systems of Equations and Inequalities: System of equations
Two or more equations considered together
Solution of a system
An ordered pair satisfying every equation in the system
Substitution method
Solving one equation for a variable and substituting into the other
Elimination method
Adding or subtracting equations to cancel one variable
Graphing method
Finding the solution as the intersection point of the graphs
Consistent system
A system with at least one solution
Inconsistent system
A system with no solution, shown by parallel lines
Dependent system
A system with infinitely many solutions, where the lines coincide
System of inequalities
Two or more inequalities whose solution is the overlapping shaded region
Feasible region
The area satisfying all inequalities in a system
Exponents and Exponential Functions: Base
The number being raised to a power
Exponent
The number of times the base is used as a factor
Product of powers
Multiplying like bases adds the exponents
Quotient of powers
Dividing like bases subtracts the exponents
Power of a power
Raising a power to a power multiplies the exponents
Zero exponent
Any nonzero base raised to the zero power equals 1
Negative exponent
Indicates a reciprocal, so x to the -n equals 1 over x to the n
Scientific notation
Writing a number as a value between 1 and 10 times a power of ten
Exponential growth
Repeated multiplication by a factor greater than 1
Exponential decay
Repeated multiplication by a factor between 0 and 1
Polynomials and Operations: Polynomial
An expression of terms with whole-number exponents on the variables
Monomial
A polynomial with exactly one term
Binomial
A polynomial with exactly two terms
Trinomial
A polynomial with exactly three terms
Degree of a polynomial
The highest exponent appearing in the expression
Leading coefficient
The coefficient of the term with the highest degree
Standard form of a polynomial
Terms written in order from highest to lowest degree
FOIL
First, Outer, Inner, Last, a method for multiplying two binomials
Difference of squares
The pattern a^2 - b^2, which factors into (a + b)(a - b)
Perfect square trinomial
A trinomial that factors into an identical pair of binomials
Factoring: Factoring
Rewriting an expression as a product of its factors
Greatest common factor
The largest factor shared by every term
Factoring by grouping
Splitting four terms into pairs and factoring each pair
Zero product property
If a product equals zero, at least one factor must be zero
Prime polynomial
A polynomial that cannot be factored further over the integers
Factoring x^2 + bx + c
Find two numbers that multiply to c and add to b
Factoring a difference of squares
Recognise a^2 - b^2 and write (a + b)(a - b)
Root of a polynomial
A value making the polynomial equal zero
Perfect cube
A number or expression that is some value raised to the third power
Completely factored
Factored until no factor can be broken down further
Quadratic Functions and Equations: Quadratic function
A function whose highest exponent is 2, graphing as a parabola
Parabola
The U-shaped graph of a quadratic function
Vertex
The highest or lowest point of a parabola
Axis of symmetry
The vertical line through the vertex that mirrors the parabola
Quadratic formula
x equals negative b plus or minus the square root of b squared minus 4ac, all over 2a
Discriminant
The expression b^2 - 4ac, which reveals the number of real roots
Completing the square
Rewriting a quadratic as a perfect square trinomial plus a constant
Zeros of a function
The x-values where the graph crosses the x-axis
Maximum value
The vertex y-value when the parabola opens downward
Minimum value
The vertex y-value when the parabola opens upward
Radicals and Rational Expressions: Radical
An expression containing a root symbol
Radicand
The value underneath the radical sign
Simplifying a radical
Removing perfect-square factors from under the root
Rationalising the denominator
Rewriting a fraction so no radical remains in the denominator
Rational expression
A fraction whose numerator and denominator are polynomials
Excluded value
A value making the denominator zero, so it is not allowed
Extraneous solution
A solution that appears algebraically but fails in the original equation
Like radicals
Radicals with the same index and radicand, which can be combined
Square root
A value that multiplied by itself gives the radicand
Cube root
A value that used three times as a factor gives the radicand
Data Analysis and Statistics: Mean
The sum of values divided by how many values there are
Median
The middle value when the data is placed in order
Mode
The value appearing most often in a data set
Range of a data set
The largest value minus the smallest value
Outlier
A value far outside the pattern of the rest of the data
Scatter plot
A graph of paired data used to look for a relationship
Line of best fit
A line drawn to model the trend in a scatter plot
Correlation
A measured relationship between two variables
Interquartile range
The spread of the middle half of the data, Q3 minus Q1
Box plot
A display showing minimum, quartiles, median, and maximum
